title: Take others' negative experiences seriously - find another pet insurance provider.
text:
Guys - don't ignore the red flags/warning signs. Embrace Pet Insurance is as close to being a scam as it gets while still remaining legal. Do not fall for the marketing. Choose a different pet insurance provider!
Read the other 1-star reviews - there's a common thread. People pay premiums for years while their pet is healthy, then the moment they need anything from Embrace, they're made to submit copious paperwork, which Embrace's claims agents then go through with a magnifying glass, broadly creating new diagnoses based on small remarks, like "scratched his ear" - oh, all ear infections are now and forevermore pre-existing. "Hind leg looks stiff" - now we will never cover any joint-related issues in any leg. When I talked to my vet about how insane all of this was, he asked me who my pet insurance was, and when I said Embrace, he rolled his eyes and told me to give up and switch, because he's had previous negative experiences trying to appeal denials with Embrace.
You can actually get a sample of the type of treatment you will get by reading their replies to these reviews. Even in their replies to Trustpilot reviews, they use carefully crafted legalese - using many words to justify denied claims that, under normal common sense, should be covered.
I've learned my lesson the hard way, cancelled my policy, and accepted that the premiums I've paid are gone forever. But if I can help you avoid the stress and frustration that comes with realizing that all the money you've put into Embrace for a peace of mind was for naught at precisely the moment you are most worried sick for your pet, then at least the money had some use after all.

title: UNETHICAL LOOPHOLES. Do NOT use Embrace!
text:
If I could give this company 0 stars I would. I enrolled in Embrace Pet Insurance through USAA in April for two cats. I added my dog later so I have been paying nearly $100/month for all 3. What I got in return was a masterclass in how to deny coverage without technically breaking the rules. One of my cats, Boots, was diagnosed with anxiety MONTHS after her policy started. That means it was not pre-existing and should have been covered. I understood I had a $500
deductible and accepted that I'd be paying out of pocket until I met it. However, TODAY 12/19/2025, when I called to ask about lowering my deductible at renewal (expecting a higher premium), I was told that any policy change would cause them to "reassess preexisting conditions" , and suddenly, her anxiety would
be considered pre-existing and excluded entirely. Let that sink in for a second... A condition that developed while insured magically becomes pre-existing if you try to adjust your coverage... This effectively traps you in the original plan and punishes you for having a pet who actually needs ongoing care. If you're buying this insurance hoping it will help with chronic conditions, behavioral meds, or long-term care, don't. It works fine if nothing ever happens. The moment you need it, or try to make your policy actually useful, the loopholes appear. Extremely disappointing, especially given the USAA partnership. I cancelled all policies and would never recommend this company to anyone who actually loves their pets.

title: FIND ANOTHER COMPANY! NOW!
text:
Embrace Pet Insurance was reliable during my cats’ early years: I have two beautiful Maine Coon cats. They are littermates, and so-in-love with each other. As Max ages, he now has a couple chronic conditions, and Embrace is sending him out to pasture.

1. Unaffordable costs: Monthly premiums almost doubled from $200+ to $380 last year! Committing to this company for 13+ years (many of which were healthy), meant nothing for our future security.

2. Fuzzy financial behavior!  
a) One cat had $200 in health credits for future Vet visits — Embrace quickly DELETED my balance! Why did they do that? ‘Because they decided to stop offering that particular benefit?’ No mention of real financial value WE lost. 

b) If I wanted to decrease my coverage last year, which was equally higher, they told me it would be a new policy, so all their health issues would become pre-existing conditions! I could make NO changes to allay costs. I could not take him to another insurance company for that same reason.

All my payments were timely and reliable. Max (and his sister Rose) were fairly healthy for many of those years. Premiums for healthy cats are ideal for any insurance company. Embrace benefited from those low-cost years. Now, everything changes due to their own desired profit margins.

I must take his sister (still healthy, but minus her $200!) off, and find her insurance elsewhere, before she has any pre-existing conditions, like Max.

I placed my trust in a what seemed to be a responsible company, and now my cat has NO insurance. Poor healthcare will emotionally impact his sister’s chances as well -- losing Max early may bring her down.

Before your cat has any illnesses that are labeled a pre-existing condition, you must find an alternate company with likely lower premiums (from what I've learned in my research).

title: I purchased Embrace Pet insurance for my German Shepherd dogs
text:
I purchased Embrace Pet insurance for two of my dogs six months ago. I researched a lot of companies and settled on Embrace. They seemed to have the best coverage for the price. The person that I signed up with on the phone originally said that they wouldn't cover any illness unless I had a Wellness Check done on my dogs. I thought that was silly considering they weren't sick, but whatever. He also told me that any accidents & injuries would be covered immediately (as in, the next day). 

Well, the next day, my German Shepherd sliced one of his paw pads really badly, so I made an appointment with my vet for the following day. By the time I got to the vet, a large portion of his paw pad had completely fallen off from the cut and he wasn't limping anymore. I was thankful. He was fine. I decided to go ahead and have a wellness check done since we were there. 

Embrace did not cover the injury because he had a wellness check and because there was supposedly a 14-day waiting period. Then I called Embrace and spoke to Derrick who checked into it and said that an accident should have been covered immediately and he would resubmit the claim.

Today, I received an email from Embrace stating that they would not cover the accident because there was a 30-day waiting period. These guys should really learn about the company they work for and get their stories straight. They also said that the vet's notes said that my mere 2-year-old German Shepherd had some tarter build-up and so that is now a pre-existing condition and they won't cover any dental for him if he has a problem. The paw pad of course, is not a pre-existing condition. And because the vet prescribed a parasite medication, they won't cover anything having to do with a parasite for at least 12 months. 

I mean, seriously? This is not how businesses should be run. I spend a lot of money on pet insurance and this company is full of a bunch of liars and scam artists. And when I was telling two of my friends about this today, they said that they had a similar experience and decided pet insurance was too expensive and cancelled their policy. When I told them that the company I was talking about was Embrace, they said, "That's the one we had!"

So, that clinched it. I'm not nuts. That was enough for me and I have decided to cancel my policies with this company and will be seeking insurance elsewhere (probably the one I have for my other dog, PetFirst with MetLife). I hope this review was helpful for people. I really do not recommend this company at all. And, btw, this is only the second one-star review I have ever given to anyone, so this is legitimately bad in my opinion.

title: Saving Bella
text:
5-Star Review for Embrace Pet Insurance
I can’t recommend Embrace Pet Insurance highly enough—it’s been a true lifesaver for my beloved cat Bella, and I wish every pet owner knew about it.
Bella has been insured with Embrace for over 11 years. For the first 10, she was the picture of health—never a single claim—and I nearly canceled the policy to save money. I’m so grateful I didn’t. Just months later, Bella was diagnosed with small cell lymphoma (SCL). We sought specialized treatment at Cornell University Veterinary Specialists for more than a year, and today, I’m overjoyed to say she’s in full remission. During that time, she was also diagnosed with hyperthyroidism and gingivitis, adding to the emotional and financial strain.
My plan has a reasonable $100 deductible, 80% reimbursement, and up to $10,000 annual coverage—perfect for comprehensive care without breaking the bank. Embrace covered diagnostics, chemotherapy, medications, specialist visits, and follow-ups promptly and fairly. Without this insurance, the costs would have been overwhelming, and I honestly don’t know if I could have afforded to give Bella the fighting chance she deserved. It might have forced a heartbreaking decision no pet parent should face.
What sets Embrace apart is their exceptional service: claims are processed quickly (often with direct deposit), medications are covered without hassle, and their staff is genuinely friendly, knowledgeable, and compassionate—answering every worried question with patience during our toughest days.
Pet insurance isn’t something you think you’ll need until you do—and when that moment comes (even after years of perfect health), Embrace is there like a safety net you didn’t know you had. Bella is thriving today because of it. If you love your pet as family, do them (and yourself) a favor: get Embrace. It’s peace of mind that turns out to be priceless.
Thank you, Embrace, for helping me save my girl’s life. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

title: Hate to have to give this rating but...
text:
Hate to have to give this rating but I have to. I have been with embrace for about 4 years. I received the quote for next year and my jaw dropped. I understand as a pet ages the cost for renewal goes up. It works the same way with humans. Every year it would go up around $100-200 but not this time. I paid about $700ish for all of 2025 and next year is about $1300ish.  Almost double, this is insane. It was this year that I discovered he has Cushing's Disease and gallbladder sludge, what a coincidence. I believe this is deceptive practice because in "pet insurance" world, if your pet has a pre-existing condition, you can't just up and leave to another insurance. I feel this is how they trap you because they know that you do not have the freedom to just up and leave. Now you just have to settle on the exorbitant price increases. 

They will hit you with this copy/paste message " Embrace evaluates our premium increases annually based on our entire book of business focusing on several factors, including the age of the insured pet(s), the tenure of the policy and also factoring in veterinary inflation. This includes not only rising veterinary costs but also the recent advances we are seeing in veterinary care. We strive to find a balance in maintaining quality coverage for the pets that we insure, while also factoring in changes in the marketplace."

This is just an excuse to lighten the blow to you. I reiterate, the reality is if your pet develops a condition under their policy, they see it as free reign to double, triple, quadruple your renewal because no other insurance will take you now. Be careful. I will be challenging this.

title: Avoid this company — they will drop your senior dog when you need them most.
text:
I was an Embrace customer for over 13 years and used to recommend them to everyone. Sadly, I can’t say that anymore.

This year, they raised the premium on my 15-year-old chihuahua from about $2,000 to over $10,000 annually — even with the multi-pet discount. The plan only pays out a maximum of $10,000 per year, so the new price makes the coverage essentially worthless. They’re pushing us off the policy without technically cancelling us.

My dog has been insured with Embrace since he was 3 and had more than a decade of healthy years with almost no issues. Now that he’s developed two conditions that count as pre-existing, no other insurer will cover him in any meaningful way. After more than a decade of loyalty, we’re left uninsured when he needs help the most.

When I called Embrace for an explanation, all I got was a canned response about “state-approved rates” and rising veterinary costs. Yes, vet care has gone up — but nothing justifies a five-fold increase in one year.

Because of this experience, I’ll also be removing my younger dog from Embrace. A company that treats long-term customers this way does not deserve our trust.

title: Customer Service Grossly Misrepresents their Policies
text:
My pet insurance policy was misrepresented to me prior to purchase, but Embrace is telling me that they don't uphold anything said by their customer service reps. I attempted to clarify a policy detail with customer service prior to purchasing the policy and they assured me that only pre-existing conditions were not covered by the policy. The reality is that any condition which the insurance company deems related to a pre-existing condition is additionally not covered by the policy. In my case, one of my cats has Entropion, which is considered a pre-existing condition since she has had it since birth. I paid for the surgery to correct it, but now Embrace informed me that any eye conditions (for example, conjunctivitis) will not be covered at all by the policy unless the vet can clearly attribute the cause to an injury or other illness. If they cannot, they will just assume the eye condition is related to the pre-existing condition (Entropion). This is a gross misrepresentation of the policy given that I explicitly asked customer service questions to try and understand what was and was not covered, and this exclusion was not mentioned to me.

EDIT: Embrace replied below to this review, but you'll notice that they totally avoided my concern. I am not disputing that Entropion is a pre-existing condition. I'm disputing the fact that Embrace does not consider it curable when in fact there is a surgery to correct it, and I am also disputing the fact that Embrace refuses to cover any future eye related issues unless they can be explicitly tied to an injury or other illness.

They do not even have a public list of what they consider to be curable and non-curable conditions, and they won't disclose this to you because it's totally at their discretion.
